representation: English research paraphrase; not normative wording
notes: All three overall grade-band descriptions and every grade-band row in Appendix1 tables25–28 are mapped. These are curriculum stage characteristics, not examination rules. Source guidance/support differences between stage rows are preserved.

summary: With teacher guidance and support, complete learning tasks, understand familiar everyday simple language, and begin developing a feel for English.
Use short basic language to interact and describe familiar things; show curiosity about Chinese and other cultures and observe family, school and community life across cultural settings.
Develop identity and national belonging, compare similarities and differences from more than one perspective, and build interest, early learning habits and willingness to collaborate.
With teacher guidance and prompting, understand common simple everyday language and communicate about relevant themes, including personal ideas.
Experience cultural diversity, learn about concrete cultural phenomena, develop national feeling and cultural confidence, and form sound values and personal qualities.
Begin thinking independently, asking questions, considering multiple perspectives critically and expressing reasoned judgments.
Adjust plans and strategies as learning progresses, identify useful personal methods, establish learning habits, explore actively and work with others.
Understand simple everyday language and communicate information, viewpoints, feelings and attitudes in everyday or general social settings.
Respect and accommodate cultural differences, compare cultural similarities and differences, broaden international outlook and strengthen national feeling.
Appreciate valued cultural meanings and develop sound values, aesthetic judgment and personal qualities.
Combine, classify, summarize, evaluate and connect information logically; think independently and identify, analyse and creatively address problems.
Try strategies, reflect and find effective personal learning methods; develop sustained habits and independent, collaborative and inquiry-based learning.
With teacher guidance and support, work within the relevant level themes to understand familiar simple everyday material and identify, extract and organize information.
Use learned language to interact, describe familiar experiences or objects and express attitudes; use imitation, repetition, gestures or facial expressions when needed.
With teacher guidance and prompting, understand common simple everyday material, its basic meaning and main content, and obtain and combine basic factual information.
Use learned language to exchange information, recount events and express attitudes and viewpoints in basic communication.
With teacher guidance and support, understand simple everyday material within the level themes, identify key or specific information and main points, and analyse or infer implied information.
Use learned language to describe phenomena and experiences, introduce familiar people or things and express viewpoints, feelings and attitudes with basic accuracy, coherence and fluency.
With teacher guidance and support, observe daily life, food and important festivals across cultures and show curiosity about Chinese and other cultures.
Use pictures and simple language material to obtain and compare basic cultural information, and use simple words or sentences to describe familiar cultural images and phenomena.
Begin recognizing cultural similarities and differences while developing identity and national belonging.
With teacher guidance and prompting, explore concrete Chinese and other cultural phenomena through common simple material such as stories, introductions, dialogue and animation.
Experience cultural diversity; briefly describe familiar cultural matters, identify with Chinese culture and recognize values or life lessons in it.
Develop sound values and personal qualities and begin comparing cultural similarities and differences.
With teacher guidance and support, use suitable methods to understand concrete cultural phenomena, respect different cultures, nurture national feeling and begin understanding a shared human future.
Obtain and summarize cultural information from simple thematic material; notice how cultural differences affect communication and try different communication strategies.

Describe familiar cultural phenomena and differences using learned English; compare and evaluate similarities and differences and appreciate valued cultural meanings, sound values, aesthetics and character.
With teacher guidance and support, observe language and cultural phenomena in learned material and identify similarities and differences.
Use available information to judge main information or viewpoints, begin recognizing problems, consider other perspectives and actively ask questions.
With teacher guidance and prompting, actively compare language and cultural phenomena, identify similarities and differences and discover or infer cause and effect.
Summarize shared features, formulate personal ideas, express reasoned views and consider others’ perspectives.
Begin evaluating matters critically and independently rather than accepting or rejecting them without thought.
With teacher guidance and support, select suitable ways to observe and understand language and cultural phenomena, compare key information and distinguish factual from nonfactual information.
Analyse and infer connections and logic, summarize main points or patterns, identify and analyse problems and progressively solve new problems creatively.
Consider multiple perspectives, think independently about viewpoints, judge information authenticity and values, and raise reasonable doubts.
With teacher guidance and support, enjoy learning English, notice differences from learning Chinese and begin recognizing pronunciation, intonation and simple spelling patterns.
Join imitation, chants, singing or performance, understand the need to speak boldly without fearing mistakes, and listen politely while expressing ideas.
Begin setting and carrying out learning plans, learn from classmates, ask for help, collaborate and form early learning habits.
With teacher guidance and prompting, recognize the importance of English and show growing interest; begin understanding how English learning works.
Try different strategies, make feasible plans, adjust plans and methods through reflection and progress, and find suitable personal approaches.
Use varied resources, develop an initial sense of independent learning and establish learning habits.
With teacher guidance and support, recognize the value of English, sustain interest and show some resilience when learning is difficult.
Understand learning patterns, try strategies, make and pursue suitable plans, reflect and adjust methods as progress develops.
Actively use libraries and other resources and develop early independent, collaborative and inquiry learning abilities and sound learning habits.
